chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Sulayman from al-Husayn ibn Umar said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Indeed, a man bequeathed to me something in the way of God,' and he said to me, 'Allocate it in Hajj.' I said to him, 'He bequeathed to me in the way of God,' and he said to me, 'Allocate it in Hajj.' I said to him, 'He bequeathed to me in the way of God,' and he said, 'Allocate it in Hajj, for I do not know anything of his way that is superior to Hajj.'

key_terms.فِي السَّبِيلِ: In the way of God (general charitable cause)

ai.seo_question: What is the preferred allocation for a bequest designated as 'in the way of God' if no specific purpose is mentioned?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the interpretation of the general term 'fi sabilillah' when no specific beneficiary is named, ruling that the funds should be directed toward Hajj. This ruling highlights the preeminence of Hajj among the various charitable causes encompassed by this phrase, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that Hajj serves as the primary vessel for this category of bequests. The repetition of the instruction underscores the certainty of this interpretation in the absence of explicit specification.
